title: Basic English — Course 1, Semester 1 — Pilot Variant 02

tasks.prompt: Listening 1. Listen to Emma. What time does the first lesson start?
tasks.audioText: Good morning. This is Emma from Group A. Our first lesson starts at nine in Room 12, not Room 21. Please bring your English notebook and the college map. At eleven, we have a short break. After lunch, our group will visit the language laboratory. The laboratory is on the second floor, next to the computer room.

tasks.prompt: Listening 2. Where is the language laboratory?

tasks.prompt: Reading 1. Read the text. Alex has a simple plan for learning English. He studies for fifteen minutes every evening. First, he reads a short text and underlines unfamiliar words. Then he checks the meaning in a dictionary and writes one example sentence. Twice a week, he listens to a short recording and writes down the main idea. He does not try to learn twenty new words at once because he wants to remember them well. How often does Alex study English?

tasks.prompt: Write 60–80 words about a typical college day. Mention when your lessons start, two subjects or activities, how you travel to college and one thing you do to practise English.
tasks.rubric: 8 points total: the response states lesson start time, at least two subjects/activities, travel to college and one English-practice activity (0–2); events are presented in a clear daily sequence (0–2); time expressions and basic present-tense grammar are used understandably (0–2); study/transport vocabulary, spelling and punctuation support clear meaning (0–2).
